description:
Operate on the quick-capture buffer queue at the vault root; flushing writes its entries into per-thread daily logs.

Global flag: --quiet suppresses info output; place it before the subcommand.

Subcommands:
  add TEXT — append an UNKNOWN entry, raw quick-capture with no thread; fails `tend` until converted
  suggest TEXT [-y] — propose a structured add-* for raw text (INTERACTIVE unless -y)
  add-text THREAD TEXT — append a TEXT entry, a free-text observation
  add-ref THREAD TARGET [SUMMARY] — append a REF entry pointing at another vault file
  add-action THREAD TEXT [--due YYYY-MM-DD] [--scheduled YYYY-MM-DD] [--priority H|M|L] [--depends UUID8] — append an ACTION entry; also reachable as `tasks add`
  list [FILTER] — show buffer with line numbers
  rm LINE_NUMBER — remove a single line by its line number
  tend — regroup by (thread, date) and validate; idempotent
  flush — tend, then write to logs and clear the buffer

Flags:
  suggest: -y auto-accept the suggestion without prompting.
  add-ref: TARGET is a wikilink target like notes/<stem> or Projects/X.
  add-action: --due YYYY-MM-DD, applied on flush plus ingest; --scheduled YYYY-MM-DD; --priority one of H, M, L; --depends 8-hex-char UUID prefix, repeatable for multiple deps.

Examples:
  ["add-text", "Projects/SGB", "Join semantics on multi-repo commits still unresolved"]
  ["add-action", "Projects/SGB", "(Riaz Arbi) Send quarterly report", "--due", "2026-06-15", "--priority", "H"]
  ["add-ref", "Projects/SGB", "notes/2026-05-27-14-30-00", "Vendor decision"]
  ["list"]

Notes:
  Never call `suggest` without -y: without it, it prompts on stdin.
  Prefer the structured add-* subcommands over `add`. UNKNOWN entries are deliberately invalid and block `flush` until removed with `rm` and re-added via the matching add-* command.
  THREAD must resolve to an existing thread file; use `threads list` to confirm before adding.
  add-* text is one argv element: '(Assignee) description' or just 'description'.
  Run `tend` to check validity before `flush`. `flush` empties the buffer and writes logs; run a no-subcommand `tasks` afterwards to convert new ACTION lines into TASK anchors.
  Line numbers from `list` shift after any `rm`, `tend` or `flush`; re-list before each `rm`.
  Exit 1 on empty text or description, or on a malformed --due, --scheduled or --depends value.
  Do not edit the buffer file directly; use these subcommands and `tend`.
